question.problem: If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{64}$ is a sample of size $n=64$ drawn from a population with mean $\mu =10$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=16,$ calculate the value of $\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}].$
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population variance ${\sigma }^{2},$ then

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu ,\,\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}.
$$

Since the population variance ${\sigma }^{2}=16$ and the sample size $n=64,$ we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}] & =\frac{16}{64} \\  & =\frac{1}{4} \\  & =0.25.\end{aligned}
$$
